	output_number(2, 0, ($SW + ($_maincontrols_counter2 * 1/100)))
	var $_input_number_8_0 = input_number(8, 0)
	if 1
		$pow = $_input_number_8_0
	if 0
		$pow = 0

xc_files.plain_code:
# README:
;This craft is configured to be easy to use, but it is a single prop and very bare bones.
;Primarily it is designed to glide, for very good efficiency on battery charge.

#Quickstart: 
; Save its current position before takeoff. After you have taken off and before flying, save the position in the air;
; this greatly enhances all experiences with it.
;scroll down and copy the code.
;press T when sitting in the cockpit.

; A/D steers rolls left and right.
; W/S steers down and up.

;TRIM:
; up-down adjusts trim for pitch
; left-right arrow adjust the trim roll; you MUST use these do succesfully perform water-takeoffs.

#Efficient flight

;Fly the craft up to an altitude of about 8-11 kilometres, and use the trim to stabilize the craft in a 
;downward slope to achieve a stable speed of at least 44 metres/second; a bit heigher up near like 9-11kilometres
; possibly 60-70ish
;Disconnect power cable to computer when not in use to preserve power, or charge.
;Some data is printed to the computer console.


#How do I see my altitude and/or my speed, without a proper cockpit?
;simple, use this code; copy past it to a HUD. it will show you in the bottom of your screen.
;press F1, click HUD, create a new hud by any name; then paste this:


var $panel = panel(bottom, 100, 70)
init
	set_cps(15) 
	
tick
	$panel.blank(color(100,100,100,100))
	$panel.write(1, 1, cyan, "" & (get("avatar_sensor_speed")) & "m/s ")	
	$panel.write(1, 10, cyan, "" & get("avatar_sensor_altitude") & "m")
